source.title: In-Distribution Consistency Regularization Improves the Generalization of Quantization-Aware Training
source.authors: Jun-Biao Pang; Tianyang Cai; Bao-Chang Zhang; Jia-Qi Wu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no apparent cutoff or garbling prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests consistency regularization for quantization-aware training on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, a new setting for the mapped versions; it reports validation accuracy and related measurements of quantized models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on quantized models trained with consistency regularization. It does not test the mapped versions' random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected generalization, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Accuracy table entries are recorded as separate rows; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates consistency regularization for quantization-aware training, without testing any supplied claim version. Its Hessian eigenvalues measure unnormalized curvature, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its relationship to measured train–test gaps. Using SGD, a fixed batch size, and convolutional architectures does not test optimizer, batch-size, or architecture comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that CR improves quantized-model generalization by promoting flatter loss landscapes, and report accuracy improvements, noise suppression, and reduced weight oscillation. They acknowledge weaker lightweight-model results and leave regression, generation, and controlling Lipschitz constants for future work. Their curvature-based interpretation does not establish V7.
record.recipe_differences: Uses consistency regularization between augmented views and quantization-aware training with an EMA teacher; the mapped claim versions concern other interventions and measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with dataset, architecture, quantization setting, availability of unlabeled data, augmentation, and CR warm-up/strength. CR is below KD for lightweight MobileNet architectures on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: CR improves several quantized classifiers' validation accuracies, with architecture-dependent exceptions relative to KD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency regularization can improve quantization-aware image-classification performance, depending on architecture, dataset, and training configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: CR suppresses prediction-output variance under Gaussian input perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency regularization can improve quantized classifiers' stability under input noise.

fits_no_version.finding: CR has smaller reported top Hessian eigenvalues than FP32 and LSQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency-regularized quantization can reduce unnormalized Hessian curvature.

record.problems: The reported experiments concern quantized image classifiers and do not directly measure the mapped versions' claims. Uncertainty estimates are not reported. Figure-based output-variance comparisons provide no text-stated numerical values. The ImageNet ResNet-50 CR table cell is blank despite a text-reported comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Other accuracy entries in Tables I–IX are not separately transcribed to keep the record focused on representative CR results, including an architecture-dependent weaker result, and central measurement results. The tables contain additional CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet settings and model/bit-width combinations.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Adding, varying, or removing dropout, including its interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, correlation with measured train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No supplied version receives a verdict. The paper cites an original source concerning sharp minima, but does not test its batch-size claim. Additional results on entropy, Lipschitz spectra, and weight oscillation also fit none of the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
